The spirit of the sea
Welcome aboard Fingal
A former Northern Lighthouse Board ship, Fingal has been lovingly transformed into a multi award-winning floating hotel, restaurant and unique wedding and events venue. On Leith’s vibrant waterfront, Fingal offers easy tram connections to Edinburgh’s city centre, including the Old Town and the Royal Mile.
A luxury hotel with all the glamour and style of a superyacht.
Europe and Scotland's Leading Boutique Hotel (World Travel Awards 2026).
Book direct to discover the best rate.
Award-Winning Hotel
Awarded Europe and Scotland's Leading Boutique Hotel (World Travel Awards 2026) and Tripadvisor’s No.1 UK ‘One of a kind’ hotel 2025, Fingal is an AA five-star hotel with a 2 AA Rosette restaurant, a world-class destination.
Discover stunning Classic, Luxury and Duplex cabins and the magnificent Skerryvore Suite, with nautical features, including a private deck area, perfect for stargazing and Champagne.
Explore the Cabins
Book Now
The Lighthouse Restaurant
Our crew warmly welcome you to the onboard Lighthouse Restaurant & Bar to relax in this truly unique maritime setting.
Serving breakfast, afternoon tea, dinner and spectacular cocktails for both non-residents and guests, the menus embrace Scotland's finest seasonal produce from local suppliers.
Awarded 2 AA Rosettes for culinary excellence.
Book Now
Christmas Gift Vouchers
The most meaningful gifts aren't things at all. They're shared moments, new experiences, and memories that linger long after the occasion has passed.
Explore Gift Vouchers
Events & Weddings
Fingal Hotel is the perfect venue for exclusive use events, weddings, private functions, product launches and corporate celebrations.
Our elegant Ballroom, with two grand sweeping staircases, can seat up to 60 people for dinner.
This enchanting room also features a removable skylight and raised gallery for music and entertainment.
Events
Sustainability
Our crew are on a journey to ensure that sustainability is front of mind, making both big and small improvements to our boutique hotel wherever possible.
Join us on our journey
FAQs
Where is Fingal located?
Fingal is in the historic Port of Leith, only 2 miles from the city centre of Edinburgh.
What is the address of Fingal?
Fingal’s address is Alexandra Dock, Leith, Edinburgh.
Which popular attractions are close to Fingal?
The famous Royal Yacht Britannia is only a short 5-minute walk away from Fingal. Queen Elizabeth II’s former floating palace is now a five-star visitor attraction located in Leith. See all five decks with your complimentary audio guide, from the State Apartments to the Crew’s Quarters, where 220 Royal Yachtsmen worked and relaxed. Discover a tour highlight, the gleaming Engine Room, and enjoy the stunning waterfront views from the Royal Deck Tearoom.
How long has Fingal been open?
Fingal has been open since 2019.
Who owns Fingal?
In July 2014, The Royal Yacht Britannia Trust (The Trust) acquired Fingal. The Trust was keen to develop an additional income stream that was not dependent on visitors to the former Royal Yacht. As overnight accommodation is not permitted on Britannia, a luxury floating hotel concept that serviced both the leisure market and helped attract more evening events to the former Royal Yacht, was developed by the Trust’s trading company: Royal Yacht Enterprises. All staff aboard both Britannia and Fingal work with passion and precision and a desire to curate truly memorable experiences for their guests.
What are some of the property amenities at Fingal?
Fingal has 23 luxurious cabins, each named after Stevenson lighthouses. The double height Ballroom can seat 60 guests or 100 can delight in a drinks reception. The Lighthouse Restaurant & Bar serves Afternoon Tea, dinner, and cocktails with the Bridge offering a space for private dining.
Is Fingal accessible?
Access from the car park or pavement is along the quayside which has a cobbled surface, and as you near the ship, in part there is a smooth, flat section. Access for all guests to board the ship is via an inclined gangway covered by an anti-slip red carpet. This leads guests to Reception, via a set of wooden double doors. If you require assistance on arrival, please let us know in advance and our staff will look out for you. Alternatively, please phone us when you arrive. There is a lift and stairs to each of the decks including The Lighthouse Restaurant & Bar, Bridge, Ballroom and accessible Classic cabin.
What are some of the room amenities at Fingal?
Each cabin on board Fingal has a king-size bed, Wi-Fi, smart TV as well as tea and coffee-making facilities. The room features a hairdryer, iron, and board. Each ensuite cabin has Noble Isle products, fluffy bathrobes and slippers.
What food and drink options are available at Fingal?
In The Lighthouse Restaurant & Bar at Fingal, guests can enjoy a delicious five-course afternoon tea of sweet and savoury delicacies. Only the best seasonal ingredients are selected by our Galley chefs, creating memorable dinner dishes, bursting with flavour. Stunning cocktails can be enjoyed under the restaurant’s shimmering ceiling. Tables must be pre-booked.
Is parking available at Fingal?
Yes, there is free parking available for guests staying at Fingal.
Are there facilities to exercise at Fingal?
There are no gym facilities on board Fingal but there is a PureGym at Ocean Terminal, just a 5-minute walk away, or David Lloyd Gym at Newhaven only a short 10-minute drive from the hotel.

Fingal offers a list of services and prices in each cabin’s wardrobe. Items received before 9.00am will be returned the same day. A complimentary shoe shine service is available on request.

The health and safety of our guests and crew is a top priority for our team at Fingal. If you would like to enquire about our procedures, please contact our reservations team who can put you in touch with our General Manager.

Our Story
The story of Fingal
01
The beginning
Fingal was commissioned by the Northern Lighthouse Board (NLB) in 1963 and was the last ship to be built by the Blythswood Shipbuilding Company in Glasgow. Registered in Leith, she was stationed for 30 years in Oban and then for 6 years in Stromness, ferrying lighthouse keepers, essential supplies and maintenance staff to lighthouses, as well as undertaking repairs to navigational aids throughout the West Coast and the North of Scotland. Fingal retired from NLB service in 2000. The name Fingal is believed to pay homage to the King of the Morven (Argyll) in ancient Caledonia during the 3rd century.
02
The maiden voyage
“The ship proved herself to be most comfortable and a very good sea boat, indeed, it is true to say that all concerned are most satisfied with her and look forward to her performing many years of useful work in the service.”
NLB Secretary W Alastair Robertson to J A Campbell Brown, Director at Blythswood Shipbuilding Company.
03
Her early days
Fingal’s duties included bringing equipment of the utmost importance to some of Scotland’s most far-off lighthouses. She was one of three vessels responsible for the Scottish coast and when lighthouse keepers saw Fingal on the horizon, it meant their three week posting was over and that replacement lighthouse keepers and vital supplies were on the way.
Discover what life was like aboard Fingal as a working ship.
Photography by Alan Provan
View the video
04
New owners
After retiring from NLB service, Fingal was sold to a private owner and renamed ‘Windsor Castle’. The proud new owner fully maintained the ship in working order for 14 years on the River Fal in Cornwall.
It was in December 2008 that Fingal's owner first approached The Royal Yacht Britannia Trust (the Trust) to enquire if it was interested in acquiring Windsor Castle. There then followed six years of negotiations before the ship was eventually acquired by the Trust in July 2014.   After a dry dock survey in Falmouth, the ship was towed to Leith in August 2014 and the detailed designs began.
Two years later her original name: Fingal was restored as a tribute to the outstanding role she had performed for the NLB, and the great affection with which she was held throughout the coastal communities she served.
View the video
05
A new life in Leith
The Royal Yacht Britannia Trust were keen to develop an additional income stream that was not dependent on visitors to the former Royal Yacht. As overnight accommodation is not permitted on Britannia, a luxury floating hotel concept that serviced both the leisure market and helped attract more evening events to the former Royal Yacht, was developed by the Trust’s trading company: Royal Yacht Enterprises.
06
A Dazzling interlude
Whilst the designs for Fingal’s conversion were being prepared in 2016, the WW1 commemorative charity, 14-18 Now, asked if they could ‘dazzle paint’ Fingal as a tribute to Royal Navy and Merchant Navy ships that had been painted to confuse enemy submariners during the First World War. As Leith Docks was home to many of these dazzle painted WW1 ships, the Trust agreed to this request, and the Turner Prize Finalist, Ciara Phillips, was commissioned to design and dazzle paint Fingal.
07
The Royal Yacht Britannia team on board
“Having excelled in the visitor attraction market for nearly 20 years, we are very much looking forward to the challenges of operating in the luxury hotel market and the benefits it will generate for BRITANNIA over the years to come.”
Bob Downie, Britannia’s founding Chief Executive .
Visit the Royal Yacht Britannia
08
A brand-new Fingal
The £5m conversion took more than two years to complete, and involved totally hollowing out the ship to create 14-bedroom cabins on the main deck, including four duplex rooms. The funnel was removed to allow two new decks to be built behind where it used to be, the lower of which would feature eight larger bedroom cabins and a Presidential Suite, while the upper would be for The Lighthouse Bar and a small private dining room, The Bridge.
The top half of the funnel was then placed on top of The Lighthouse Restaurant & Bar deck to give the appearance that it was part of the original construction.
The conversion also included a spectacular round glass lift for the guests, and a separate back of house lift and stairwell for staff which connected the main galley to the four decks above, meaning they could access all areas from ‘behind the scenes’.
Fingal Hotel, the luxury floating hotel, opened to the public in January 2019. Her new life had truly begun.
09
Legacy of Scottish lighthouses
The Stevenson family was responsible for designing all of Scotland’s lighthouses, so to credit their work, and the NLB, each of the 23 cabins aboard Fingal are named after their lighthouses. The photographs of lighthouses that you see today on Fingal were all taken by a pharologist: Ian Cowe whose passion was to photograph every one of the Stevenson lighthouses in Scotland and the Isle of Man that were operated by the Northern Lighthouse Board. You can see more of Ian’s work in his book: Scottish and Manx Lighthouses: A Photographic Journey in the Footsteps of the Stevensons.
View Ian s Portfolio
Skerryvore
The Skerryvore Lighthouse is renowned as one of the most beautiful lighthouses in the world, so it was only fitting that our most lavish cabin on board be named after it. The Skerryvore Suite provides an unparalleled experience of indulgence, taking luxury to a whole new level.
Robert Stevenson's talented family also included the famous Scottish writer Robert Louis Stevenson (Robert's grandson). Probably inspired by visits with his grandfather to remote lighthouses, RL Stevenson wrote of many dramatic sea tales in his books Treasure Island and Kidnapped.

Luxury Cabin
Sleep beautifully
For an unforgettable experience. Gaze out across the water and watch the twinkling city lights before curling up in the spectacular luxury of your cabin. S umptuous heritage fabrics created by Scottish textile designer Araminta Campbell tell the Fingal Hotel's story. The purple heather of the Scottish mountain landscape, a bright light casting the warm glow of the lighthouse beam, guarding ships safely away from the rocky shores.
Little features such as a headboard with map contours to trace, Davy lamps and heavy brass taps, make for a stay that will continue to inspire, long after you've left.

Reviews
Exceptional from start to finish
The most luxurious place I have ever stayed. The attention to detail is phenomenal and the rooms, food, service were all exceptional. It doesn’t feel like you are on a boat (my husband had been worried as he gets seasick) but the nautical elements and history are fascinating. Very impressed and highly recommend.
Read the full review
Exceeded all expectations
I surprised my wife with a one-night stay as a special treat for our 10-year anniversary and it was such an incredible and unique experience. With the included Britannia tickets and full Scottish breakfast, it far exceeded our expectations. We also did the afternoon tea which was an experience of its own. The staff were friendly, the amenities were incredible, and the local tram is just out the door. This was by far the most lavish experience either of us have had and definitely checked off every box we could have imagined.
Read the full review
Heaven on earth . Truly amazing
Such a wonderful hotel. Afternoon tea was the best ever. Staff so amazing, catering to every need . Best experience ever and food was truly outstanding.

FAQ
Do you have any mobile offers?
Yes, we currently offer up to 15% off when you book within 7 days of arrival in advance, only available through your mobile device.
Can the windows be opened?
No.
Is there a bath in the cabin?
Only Luxury Duplex Suites & Skerryvore Suite (both have freestanding baths as well as separate rainfall showers) – all others have walk-in rainfall showers.
Can you accommodate any extra beds in the cabin?
No, our rooms are suitable for a maximum of 2 adults and we cannot add any extra beds.
Can the room be set with twin beds?
Only 4 of our Classic Cabins can be set up as a twin room (2 single beds). All other cabins/suites have solid double beds (king, super king or emperor depending on the room).
Can I access the deck space from my cabin?
Luxury Cabins have doors leading directly from the cabin onto the shared outdoor deck space. Our Skerryvore Suite has a private deck space. All other cabins do not have direct deck access, but this can be accessed via the communal corridors.
Does the cabin have a view?
We’d recommend the Luxury Cabins as having the best views, otherwise most rooms have limited views due to portholes and location.
Can I order room service to my cabin?
Yes, we can provide room service during our restaurant opening hours, with guests ordering from our restaurant menus. Please note the only room with a dining table is Skerryvore, so it is recommended to take meals in the restaurant for a more comfortable dining experience (particularly for Afternoon Tea or dinner).
Is there milk in the mini bar?
We do not leave milk in the mini-bars however fresh milk can be requested and we will deliver this to your cabin.
Is there an iron/ironing board in the cabin?
Yes.
Is there a hairdryer in the cabin?
Yes.
Are toiletries in the cabin?
Yes, we provide shampoo, conditioner, shower gel, and moisturiser.
Do you have a laundry service?
Yes we can organise this for you, charges apply.

wikipedia.extract: MV Fingal is a former Northern Lighthouse Board ship converted into a boutique hotel. Fingal is permanently berthed relatively near the former Royal Yacht Britannia as part of a major tourist attraction in Edinburgh, Scotland.
